title: (RHBA-2015:2069) openstack-neutron bug fix advisory
portal_summary:
Updated OpenStack Networking packages that resolve various issues are now
available for Red Hat Enterprise Linux OpenStack Platform 6.0 (Juno) for
RHEL 7.
portal_product_filter: Red Hat OpenStack Platform|Red Hat OpenStack|6.0|x86_64
portal_solution:
Before applying this update, ensure all previously released errata relevant to your system have been applied.

Red Hat Enterprise Linux OpenStack Platform 6 runs on Red Hat Enterprise Linux 7.1.

The Red Hat Enterprise Linux OpenStack Platform 6 Release Notes (see the References section) contain the following:
* An explanation of the way in which the provided components interact to form a working cloud computing environment.
* Technology Previews, Recommended Practices, and Known Issues.
* The channels required for Red Hat Enterprise Linux OpenStack Platform 6, including which channels need to be enabled and disabled.

This update is available through the Red Hat Network. Details on how to use the Red Hat Network to apply this update are available at https://access.redhat.com/site/articles/11258
portal_description:
Red Hat Enterprise Linux OpenStack Platform provides the facilities for
building a private or public infrastructure-as-a-service (IaaS) cloud
running on commonly available physical hardware. This advisory includes
packages for:

* OpenStack Networking service

OpenStack Networking (neutron) is a virtual network service for OpenStack.
Just as OpenStack Compute (nova) provides an API to dynamically request and
configure virtual servers, OpenStack Networking provides an API to
dynamically request and configure virtual networks. These networks connect
'interfaces' from other OpenStack services (e.g. virtual NICs from Compute
VMs).  The OpenStack Networking API supports extensions to provide advanced
network capabilities (e.g. QoS, ACLs, network monitoring, etc.)

Changes to the openstack-neutron component:

* Cause: network service calls ovs-ifdown lsb script that issues del-br on all bridges in ovsdb that leads to loss of information about its ports, which were veth pairs between integration and external bridges.

Consequence: if network service is restarted, then external bridge is re-created without configuration done by Neutron, leading to losing connectivity to external network

Fix: restart of network service now triggers restart of neutron-openvswitch-agent that syncs all its ports upon startup

Result: veth pairs are re-created after neutron-openvswitch-agent is started and external connectivity works. IMPORTANT NOTE: if l3_agent.ini configures external_network_bridge then qg- device managed by l3-agent is not re-created and administrator must manually restart neutron-l3-agent service on the node where network service was restarted. bridge_mappings are recommended to be used instead of external_network_bridge. (BZ#1275732)
